_about: match_rules rule 5 (qualifier_conflict): a word in a requirement's SUBJECT that says WHICH side, part or location of a quantity it is about. When the subject carries one and the datasheet field name does not, the pairing is refused ('the maximum external design pressure' is not the sheet's 'Design pressure'; 'the operating pressure of the jacket' is not its 'Operating pressure'). Found on the real PSV review, 2026-10-10. Generic: no standard, document or equipment named. A refusal leaves the requirement unpaired (an engineer's question), never a verdict, so a word here errs towards caution. Checked only next to the field's own words (before them, or after through 'of (the)'). 'nozzle' is NOT a qualifier: a nozzle is the item a field names (N1 size), not a side of it. derived_after: a word RIGHT AFTER the field's own words that makes it a different quantity ('set pressure TOLERANCE' is not the sheet's 'Set pressure'; 'pressure DROP' is not 'Pressure'). Found when the F-b re-read gave the PSV's set pressures values: two ASME VIII tolerance rules read COMPLIANT against the set pressure itself.
_about_quantity_kind: match_rules rule 6 (same quantity kind, order 139): a requirement pairs only with a datasheet value of the same quantity kind. quantity_nouns: the noun that NAMES a quantity, mapped to the claims.unit_dimension family its units already belong to - a LIST when the quantity is stated in more than one (vibration as a velocity or a displacement, flow as a volume or a mass per time), and a noun never refuses a unit that gives one of its kinds (claims holds the units; this holds only the words) - read only when a side states no unit (a statement, a blank field). Two different kinds refuse the pair; a kind that cannot be told, or a subject or medium word the field does not share ('weld joint' efficiency, 'flushing liquid' temperature), holds the pair for an engineer - never a verdict. subject_nouns: nouns naming ANOTHER THING whose quantity a requirement states - a medium (liquid, oil, steam) or a component with its own quantities (joint, seal, bearing). 'weld' is not one: a weld joint is the joint a datasheet's 'Joint efficiency' already names. One of these before the field's words that the field does not share holds the pair for an engineer; an adjective or state word (rated, normal, design, operating, maximum) or a part of the same equipment (shaft, casing) never does. Generic: no standard, document or equipment named. phrase_end: words that end the noun phrase naming a quantity ('the width OF the bearing surface'); determiners: words that open one and mean nothing of their own; generic_heads: words that end a phrase without naming its quantity.
